label: rem:torus-knot-shell-binding-interpretation
title: Torus-knot mediation of inter-shell crossings
html:
Withdrawn. The shell-size rule used here, that a closing shell of size n_s is bound by the torus knot T_{2,n_s}, is withdrawn. Its basis was a mislabel: (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_0 closes to T(2,4), not to the cinquefoil T(2,5). The rule stays withdrawn until it is derived. The interpretation below describes the withdrawn proposal.

When a nuclear shell closes (indicated by a palindromic Poincaré histogram), the next nucleon cannot enter the closed shell. It must start a new shell. The inter-shell crossing is mediated by a torus knot operator T_{2,k} whose index k equals the size of the closed shell. This proposition formalizes the inductive construction across shell boundaries and derives the magic numbers from the torus knot hierarchy.
